domain_label: Classic-Luxurious Genre Bible — Visual Codes (Materials, Palette, Typography, Car Canon, Accessories, Gauche Tells)
purpose: A method for the units of expert visual-styling work a classic-luxurious ('quiet luxury') genre reviewer performs: locking the quiet-vs-loud register, fixing the materials/palette/typography/composition codes that make a frame read high-end, casting cars/watches/accessories/table settings against a sourced classic-vs-flash canon with the trademark-caution boundary held open pending the likeness/rights file, and naming the gauche tells - branding/saturation, light/material, flex-grammar/casting - that break the luxury read and hand off into realism QC, each claim carried with the grounding file's own FACT/FACT-lite/ESTIMATE/UNKNOWN tag rather than invented.
assumptions: no live production dataset or per-shot QC revlog is supplied; every score is a heuristic prior, and every named fact is carried with the grounding research file's own FACT/FACT-lite/ESTIMATE/UNKNOWN tag, never invented
Higgsfield model names, ids, parameters, durations, aspect ratios, and media roles are entirely out of scope for this KB; no Higgsfield-specific detail is asserted anywhere in these nodes

the trademark/likeness legal boundary (which marks, model names, or venue names may be depicted, and how prominently) is not resolved here; every car/watch node defers to the separate likeness/rights research file and states only a conservative default posture

quiet-luxury sourcing is drawn from search-result excerpts and publisher/brand pages fetched in the grounding research session; where a figure is vendor-published (e.g. Monotype's own perception-uplift percentages) rather than independently verified, that caveat travels with the claim

the fitness-accent, location-library, and scenario-bank content the grounding file also covers belongs to other movie_studio specialists (story/cine/character); this KB scopes strictly to the visual-code/materials/palette/typography/car/accessory/gauche-tell surface named in its brief
exclusions: the location library and seasonal/time-of-day rotation logic (media-manager/cine specialist scope)
the lifestyle scenario bank and persona-alternation editorial logic (story specialist scope)
the fitness-accent integration and physique-presentation guidance (character/story specialist scope)
the generic AI-artifact taxonomy beyond the five luxury-specific intersections named in REALISM_QC_HANDOFF (the realism/QC specialist's own KB owns the full taxonomy)
any guidance for evoking a specific real person's likeness while concealing or altering the face - a closed lane, out of scope entirely, not merely deprioritized
the final legal determination on trademark/trade-dress depiction - deferred to the likeness/rights research file
Higgsfield-specific model names, ids, parameters, durations, aspect ratios, or media roles - out of scope entirely

glossary.definition: A recognized aesthetic (synonyms: stealth wealth, old money aesthetic, silent luxury) defined by understated design, high-quality materials, timeless styling, muted colors, craftsmanship, and deliberate avoidance of conspicuous logos and flashy status markers [FACT - Wikipedia "Quiet luxury"].

The contrasting register: vibrant palettes, eye-catching patterns, prominently displayed branding, and statement/sequin pieces designed to be the centerpiece [FACT - Baltini]. Out of genre except as a deliberate rare contrast beat.

Kapferer & Bastien's marketing text (Kogan Page): luxury inverts normal marketing - scarcity over reach, no discounting, price follows luxury rather than luxury following price; luxury communicates identity and heritage, not features [FACT - publisher page; the 24 anti-laws are read via a secondary summary, not the primary text].

The Rolls-Royce hood mascot designed by Charles Sykes in 1911, a "flying lady" leaning into the wind with her gown billowing; a global symbol of luxury and a protected trade-dress mark [FACT - Wikipedia; Rolls-Royce official page].

The 230/250/280 SL (1963-71), designed by Paul Bracq/Béla Barényi, whose patented slightly concave hardtop gave it the "Pagoda" nickname; widely treated as a timeless-design collectible [FACT - Wikipedia; Classic & Sports Car].

The Japanese aesthetic principle, sourced here from ryokan design coverage, that the patina of age is the highest beauty; operationally: too-new, zero-patina props read staged/AI while worn, hand-finished surfaces read owned [FACT for the ryokan sourcing - insidekyoto.com; ESTIMATE for the general staged-vs-owned extrapolation].

The forest-green + gold + black premium color combination named in branding-design literature as one of three repeatedly-cited premium combinations, alongside black+gold+ivory and navy+platinum/silver+cream [FACT - digiquack].
A named luxury-branding mistake: cluttered feeds, abandoned white space, gradient-heavy ornament-stuffed graphics [FACT - katemale.com; digiquack; mediaboom].

The reference brand list this KB never shows logos of but uses as the visual-grammar anchor: Loro Piana, Brunello Cucinelli, Zegna, Hermès, Brioni, The Row, Bottega Veneta, Celine (Philo era), Valextra; Loro Piana's signature move is a ~$5,000 cashmere blazer with no visible branding beyond an interior label [FACT - sociallifemagazine.com].

Car grilles, badges, mascots (e.g. Spirit of Ecstasy) and model trade dress, and by extension watch dial/case designs, are protected marks; whether and how prominently AI-generated commercial content may depict them is a legal question this KB defers to the separate likeness/rights research file [ESTIMATE - high that a conservative default posture is the safer lane; law pinned elsewhere].

nodes.definition: Lock the genre's register. "Quiet luxury" (synonyms: stealth wealth, old money aesthetic, silent luxury) is a recognized aesthetic defined by understated design, high-quality materials, timeless styling, muted colors, craftsmanship, and the deliberate avoidance of conspicuous logos and flashy status markers [FACT - Wikipedia "Quiet luxury"]. The register was mass-popularized by HBO's Succession, where unbranded expensive clothing (Loro Piana caps, Tom Ford suede) reads as wealth only to a trained eye, and "old money"/"stealth wealth" trended massively on TikTok in 2023 [FACT - Hypebeast; Fortune]. Loud luxury is defined by vibrant palettes, eye-catching patterns, prominently displayed branding, and statement pieces designed to be the centerpiece [FACT - Baltini]. Operating definition for this KB: classic luxurious = quiet-luxury visual grammar + cinematic execution; loud-luxury elements (logo walls, hypercar flash, champagne-spray, cash/watch-flex poses) are OUT of genre except as deliberate rare contrast beats.

included: the operating definition locking the genre
excluded: specific material/palette/typography instantiations (their own nodes)
the rare-contrast-beat exception mechanics (car/gauche-tell nodes)

pros.claim: A single sourced register definition prevents every downstream specialist from drifting into an invented luxury aesthetic
pros.example: checking a wardrobe or set-design choice against the Wikipedia-sourced quiet-luxury definition rather than a vague 'looks rich' intuition

cons.claim: The register lock is sourced from a fast-moving fashion-trend discourse (2023 TikTok wave) that press already called dated by Jan-2024
cons.example: treating the 2023 TikTok-era brand list as permanently canonical when the press itself flagged the trend's peak as fading

failure_modes: shooting loud-luxury markers (logo walls, cash flex) as if they were in-genre default rather than a rare deliberate exception
treating the trend-fade caution as license to abandon quiet-luxury codes rather than reframe them as timeless grammar
acceptance_tests: the analysis states the quiet-luxury definition, the loud-luxury contrast, the Succession/TikTok sourcing, and the operating definition locking loud elements to rare contrast beats only
revisit_triggers: a scene's styling is checked against the register lock and found ambiguous
fashion press declares a further shift beyond the 2024 trend-fade note
a new specialist requests the operating definition for a styling decision

base.update_signal: fashion press declares quiet luxury further dated or superseded by a new named register

nodes.definition: Ground the operation's marketing logic in Kapferer & Bastien's The Luxury Strategy (Kogan Page): luxury inverts normal marketing - scarcity over reach, no discounting, "it is not the price that makes luxury, but luxury that makes the price"; luxury communicates identity and heritage, not features [FACT - Kapferer & Bastien publisher page; secondary 24-anti-laws summary]. Genre implication: our content sells a world, never a product pitch - a shot's job is to make the viewer feel the character's identity and heritage, not to enumerate a product's features.

excluded: specific composition rules that implement this (its own node)
material/color/car instantiations

pros.claim: Anchoring in a named published theory keeps every styling choice traceable to a stated principle rather than ad hoc taste
pros.example: justifying a shot's lack of product-feature framing by citing the identity-over-features anti-law rather than personal preference

cons.claim: The book's 24 anti-laws were read via a secondary summary rather than the primary text itself for the exhaustive list
cons.example: citing all 24 anti-laws by number when only the publisher page and one secondary summary were fetched

failure_modes: framing a shot as a product pitch (features, price, availability) instead of identity/heritage
treating the secondary summary's exact wording as if it were the book's own text
acceptance_tests: the analysis states the scarcity/no-discount/price-follows-luxury anti-laws and the identity-over-features framing, citing the publisher page and flagging the secondary-summary basis for the anti-laws list
revisit_triggers: the primary book text becomes directly available for the full 24-law list
a shot's brief is found drifting toward a product-feature pitch
a new specialist needs the identity/heritage framing for a fitness or accessory beat

base.update_signal: the primary book text becomes fetchable for the full anti-laws list

nodes.definition: Carry the trend-fade caution honestly and resolve it. By Jan-2024, fashion press called peak "quiet luxury" outdated as runway styles regained flair [FACT - Wikipedia "Quiet luxury"]. This KB's resolution: adopt quiet luxury as a timeless visual grammar (old-money codes predate and outlive the TikTok trend), not as a trend-chasing label [ESTIMATE - medium-high confidence; basis: old-money aesthetic's persistence across decades per the quiet-luxury and old-money-aesthetic sources]. Practically: production should not treat a 2023-TikTok-specific reference (a particular influencer's exact styling) as canon, but the underlying decades-old codes (unbranded natural fibers, muted palettes, heritage marques) as durable.

excluded: the specific durable codes themselves (materials/palette/car nodes)

pros.claim: Naming the trend-fade caution explicitly prevents the operation from over-indexing on a single 2023 TikTok moment that press already called dated
pros.example: choosing a decades-old Loro Piana-style unbranded cashmere code over a specific 2023 influencer's exact outfit

cons.claim: The timeless-grammar resolution is an ESTIMATE, not a fetched claim, so it should not be overstated as settled fact
cons.example: asserting 'quiet luxury will never date' as verified rather than the medium-high-confidence craft judgment it is

failure_modes: treating a 2023-specific TikTok reference as permanently canonical
overstating the timeless-grammar resolution as FACT rather than the ESTIMATE it is
acceptance_tests: the analysis states the 2024 trend-fade press finding as FACT and the timeless-grammar resolution as an explicitly-tagged ESTIMATE with its confidence level
revisit_triggers: fashion press publishes a further verdict on quiet luxury's staying power
a production choice is found over-indexing on a dated 2023-specific reference
runway/fashion trend data becomes available to test the timeless-grammar ESTIMATE

base.update_signal: fashion press publishes a further verdict on quiet luxury's durability

nodes.definition: Fix the generator-facing materials whitelist. Quiet-luxury material canon: fine natural fibers (cashmere, vicuña, baby cashmere, linen, silk, fine merino), full-grain leather, craftsmanship-forward finishes [FACT - sociallifemagazine.com; Baltini]. Interior/set materials that read high-end in luxury design coverage: marble, aged/dark woods (mahogany-class), terracotta, hand-painted ceramic tile, wrought iron, brass, natural stone, hand-poured terrazzo, hinoki, tatami, washi/shoji paper screens [FACT - designeersclub.com; hoteldesigns.net; avantgardeaspen.com; insidekyoto.com]. The generator-facing whitelist synthesized from this canon: marble (honed preferred over polished), mahogany/walnut, linen, full-grain leather, cashmere/wool, unlacquered brass, crystal, bone china, natural stone, aged hardwood floors, silk [ESTIMATE - high confidence, basis the sourced canon above].

included: the sourced fine-fiber and set-material canon
excluded: the blacklist of materials that break the read (its own node)

pros.claim: A concrete whitelist gives prompt-writers and set designers a checkable list instead of a vague 'looks expensive' instruction
pros.example: specifying 'honed marble counter, walnut cabinetry, linen napkins' in a prompt rather than 'luxurious kitchen'

cons.claim: The whitelist is an ESTIMATE synthesis, not itself a single fetched source, so its exact boundary requires craft judgment case by case
cons.example: debating whether a specific glassware piece counts as 'crystal' under the whitelist without a definitive sourced boundary

failure_modes: defaulting to polished rather than honed marble, reading showroom-flashy
treating the ESTIMATE-tagged whitelist as an exhaustive verified list rather than a craft synthesis
acceptance_tests: the analysis lists the fine-fiber canon, the set-material canon, and the 11-item generator-facing whitelist with the honed-marble preference
revisit_triggers: a new material is proposed for a set/wardrobe and needs classification against the whitelist
a sourced material canon update changes the underlying list
the blacklist is revised and the whitelist boundary needs re-checking

base.update_signal: a new sourced material canon or a set/wardrobe classification dispute arises

nodes.definition: Fix the materials blacklist that breaks the luxury read. Loud-luxury contrast: vibrant palettes, eye-catching patterns, prominently displayed branding, statement/sequin pieces designed to be the centerpiece [FACT - Baltini]. The generator-facing blacklist synthesized from the whitelist's inverse plus the gauche-tell sourcing: visible plastic, chrome-everything, acrylic furniture, glossy laminate, synthetic satin sheen [ESTIMATE - high confidence, basis the sourced canon]. Plastic/synthetic surfaces in frame (acrylic chairs, PVC, glossy laminate, polyester sheen) are named as a luxury-breaking tell [ESTIMATE - high, direct inversion of the material codes]. Any set/wardrobe element proposed for a shot is checked against this blacklist before it is approved.

included: the synthesized blacklist (plastic, chrome-everything, acrylic, glossy laminate, synthetic satin)
excluded: the light/patina gauche-tell instances (its own node)

pros.claim: An explicit blacklist gives a fast reject-list check before a prop or surface is approved for a shot
pros.example: rejecting an acrylic dining chair from a table-setting beat because it appears on the blacklist

cons.claim: The blacklist inverts the whitelist rather than being independently sourced, so edge materials require judgment
cons.example: deciding whether a lacquered brass fixture (shinier than the whitelist's unlacquered brass) counts as blacklisted chrome-adjacent shine

failure_modes: approving a glossy laminate or acrylic prop because it wasn't explicitly named
treating a borderline material (lacquered vs unlacquered brass) without applying the whitelist's stated preference
acceptance_tests: the analysis states the loud-luxury material contrast and the five-item blacklist, and states the check-before-approval discipline
revisit_triggers: a borderline material (lacquered brass, cut glass) needs a blacklist/whitelist ruling
a produced shot is flagged for a blacklisted material that slipped through
the whitelist is revised and the blacklist's inverse relationship needs re-deriving

base.update_signal: a borderline material ruling or a slipped-through blacklisted prop surfaces

nodes.definition: Fix the core palette principle. Luxury palettes rely on deep anchors (black, charcoal, navy), warm neutrals (ivory, champagne, beige, cream), and one restrained metallic accent (gold/brass); restraint itself is the luxury signal - "fewer colors equal higher perceived value" [FACT - zoviz.com; digiquack.com]. Quiet luxury specifically favors beige, gray, navy, black, and muted greens (sage/olive family) [FACT - Baltini; effortlessgent.com]. Locked grade palette for the operation: warm neutrals (cream/sand/ivory) + one deep anchor per scene (navy, forest green, charcoal, or burgundy) + gold/brass accents ≤5% of frame; saturation kept low-to-moderate, skin tones natural, whites slightly warm and never clipped [ESTIMATE - high confidence, basis above].

included: the locked grade-palette rule with the <=5% accent cap
excluded: the three specific named premium color combinations (its own node)

pros.claim: A quantified accent cap (<=5% of frame) turns a vague 'restrained gold' instruction into a checkable grading target
pros.example: a colorist checking that gold/brass pixels occupy under 5% of a graded frame before approving it

cons.claim: The <=5% cap is a craft-synthesis ESTIMATE, not a measured industry standard, so it is a starting discipline rather than a verified threshold
cons.example: treating 5% as a hard verified number when it is this KB's own operational synthesis

failure_modes: letting a gold/brass accent dominate more than the intended sliver of frame
clipping whites or oversaturating skin tones and losing the natural, restrained grade
acceptance_tests: the analysis states the deep-anchor/warm-neutral/metallic-accent principle, the restraint-equals-value finding, and the locked grade-palette rule with its <=5% accent cap
revisit_triggers: a graded shot's accent coverage is measured and found over the 5% cap
a new sourced palette-psychology finding updates the restraint principle
a scene's saturation is found clipping or oversaturating skin tones

base.update_signal: a graded shot's measured accent coverage or a new palette-psychology source updates the restraint rule

nodes.definition: Name the three specific premium combinations repeatedly cited in branding-design literature: black + gold + ivory; navy + platinum/silver + cream; forest/deep green + gold + black (the "Rolex palette") [FACT - digiquack.com]. Deep burgundy also recurs in premium identities [FACT - digiquack.com]. These combinations are applied as instances of the restraint principle (COLOR_PALETTE_CORE), not as license to use all three colors at equal saturation/weight in one frame - the accent color still stays under the ≤5%-of-frame cap.

included: the three named combinations plus burgundy
the constraint that they instantiate, not override, the restraint principle
excluded: the base restraint principle itself (its own node)

pros.claim: Naming three specific, sourced combinations gives a production designer concrete starting palettes instead of inventing new ones per scene
pros.example: choosing the navy+platinum+cream combination for a Monaco-night table setting rather than devising an unsourced palette

cons.claim: Using a named combination can tempt equal-weight application of all its colors, breaking the restraint principle it is supposed to instantiate
cons.example: lighting a scene with equally-saturated forest-green walls, gold trim and black furniture all at once instead of one anchor plus a sliver of accent

failure_modes: applying all three colors of a named combination at equal saturation/weight instead of one anchor plus a restrained accent
inventing a fourth 'premium' combination not in the sourced list
acceptance_tests: the analysis names all three combinations plus burgundy and states that each must still respect the restraint principle's accent cap
revisit_triggers: a new sourced premium color-combination finding is published
a produced shot stacks more than one combination in the same frame
a combination's accent coverage is measured and found over cap

base.update_signal: a new sourced combination or a stacked-combination production error surfaces

nodes.definition: Fix the typography system for posters, covers, and quote cards. Luxury branding leans on classical serif typefaces (Caslon/Baskerville lineage) evoking timeless sophistication; Monotype's own published research links this typography style to higher perceived quality (+13%) and reliability (+9%) - figures from Monotype's published summary, not independently verified [FACT with a vendor-reported caveat - Monotype resource page]. Refined geometric or humanist sans-serifs are the accepted alternative [FACT - Monotype]. Text rules for covers/quote cards: one serif family (Didone or old-style), letter-spaced small caps for kickers, no drop shadows, no gradients, no more than 2 type sizes per card, text occupying <20% of frame, cream-on-charcoal or charcoal-on-cream [ESTIMATE - high confidence, basis above].

included: the serif-lineage typography convention and the vendor-reported +13%/+9% caveat
the concrete text rules for cover/quote cards
excluded: the composition conventions the typography sits within (its own node)

pros.claim: Concrete card rules (one serif family, <=2 sizes, <20% frame coverage) give an editor a checkable spec instead of a vague 'elegant font' instruction
pros.example: rejecting a quote card that uses three type sizes and a drop shadow against these explicit rules

cons.claim: The headline perception-uplift figures are Monotype's own vendor-published numbers, not independently verified, so they should not be cited as neutral research
cons.example: citing '+13% perceived quality' as an independently verified academic finding rather than a vendor's own reported summary

failure_modes: citing the Monotype uplift percentages as independently verified rather than vendor-reported
using more than two type sizes or a drop-shadowed gradient headline on a cover card
acceptance_tests: the analysis states the serif-lineage convention, the vendor-reported caveat on the +13%/+9% figures, and the concrete card text rules
revisit_triggers: an independent (non-vendor) typography-perception study becomes available
a produced cover card violates the type-size or frame-coverage rule
a new sans-serif alternative is proposed and needs classification

base.update_signal: an independent typography-perception study becomes available or a card violates the stated rules

nodes.definition: Fix composition conventions for luxury advertising-style frames. Luxury layout discipline: generous white space, 2-3 tones max, minimal elements; gradients and ornament-cluttered logos read cheap [FACT - digiquack.com; mediaboom.com]. Cluttered feeds and "design noise" are named luxury-branding mistakes [FACT - katemale.com]. Composition conventions synthesized from these: symmetry or strong single-subject placement, deep negative space, low prop count (3-5 significant objects max), shallow depth of field on details, wide establishing frames on places [ESTIMATE - medium-high confidence, basis luxury advertising conventions above].

included: the synthesized composition rules (symmetry, negative space, 3-5 prop cap, shallow DoF, wide establishing frames)
excluded: the typography-specific card rules (its own node)

pros.claim: A numeric prop-count cap (3-5 significant objects) gives a set dresser a checkable limit instead of an open-ended 'keep it clean' note
pros.example: removing extra flowers, extra glassware, and a stray phone from a table-setting frame to land at 4 significant objects

cons.claim: The 3-5 object cap and the specific DoF/framing rules are an ESTIMATE synthesis, not a directly counted industry standard
cons.example: treating '3-5 objects' as a verified rule rather than this KB's own craft synthesis of the white-space/minimalism principle

failure_modes: overcrowding a frame past the 3-5 significant-object cap
using a cluttered ornament-heavy graphic overlay that reads as design noise
acceptance_tests: the analysis states the white-space/2-3-tone/minimal-element discipline, the design-noise mistake, and the synthesized composition rules with the 3-5 object cap
revisit_triggers: a produced frame is found overcrowded past the object cap
a new sourced luxury-design-mistake finding refines the design-noise category
a place-establishing frame's composition needs a wide-frame ruling

base.update_signal: an overcrowded produced frame or a new design-noise finding refines these rules

nodes.definition: Fix the classic-luxurious car canon (in-genre core). Rolls-Royce (esp. classic Silver Cloud/Corniche era and modern Ghost/Phantom in muted colors) - the Spirit of Ecstasy mascot (Charles Sykes, 1911) is the brand's iconic ornament and a global symbol of luxury [FACT - Wikipedia; Rolls-Royce official]; signature exterior: upright Pantheon-style grille, long bonnet, rear-hinged coach doors on modern cars; interiors: lambswool carpet, book-matched veneer, thin-rim wheel [FACT-lite]. Bentley (Continental, Flying Spur, classic R-Type/S-series) - matrix/mesh grille, winged-B badge, quilted leather, knurled metal [FACT-lite]. Vintage Porsche 911 (air-cooled, 1960s-80s) - unbroken fastback roofline, round headlamps, Fuchs wheels [FACT-lite; ESTIMATE that vintage-analog objects read as connoisseur signals, basis quiet-luxury press]. Mercedes SL W113 "Pagoda" (230/250/280 SL, 1963-71) - designed by Paul Bracq/Béla Barényi, patented concave hardtop, aluminium bonnet/boot/door skins, widely treated as a timeless-design collectible [FACT - Wikipedia; Classic & Sports Car]. Ferrari 250-era classics (250 GT Lusso, 250 GT California Spyder class) - Pininfarina-designed/Scaglietti-built Lusso widely regarded among the most beautiful cars ever made; the 250 GTO set the classic-car value record (~$70M private sale, 2018) [FACT - RM Sotheby's; Wikipedia]. Acceptable supporting cast: Jaguar E-Type, Aston Martin DB5/DB6, Land Rover Defender/Series (estate context), Mercedes G-Class in matte/dark (modern, borderline) [ESTIMATE - medium-high, same design-era logic].

included: the five named core marques/eras with their signature details
excluded: the flash tier and its exclusion (its own node)
the on-camera treatment/trademark caution (their own nodes)

pros.claim: A named five-marque core canon with cited signature details gives a casting decision a concrete, sourced shortlist instead of an open 'pick an expensive car' brief
pros.example: casting a Pagoda SL for a coastal-drive beat instead of an arbitrary modern luxury sedan

cons.claim: Some signature-detail claims (interior materials, grille style) are FACT-lite common-knowledge rather than directly cited to a specific fetched source
cons.example: describing Bentley's quilted-leather interior as FACT-lite general brand knowledge rather than a specific citation

failure_modes: casting a car from outside the five-marque core/supporting-cast list without checking it against the flash-tier exclusion
treating the G-Class's borderline modern status as a full classic-tier inclusion rather than the ESTIMATE-flagged borderline case it is
acceptance_tests: the analysis names the five core marques/eras with at least one signature detail each, the supporting-cast list, and the G-Class borderline flag
revisit_triggers: a new car is proposed for a shoot and needs classic-vs-flash classification
the Spirit of Ecstasy or another marque's trademark status is clarified by the likeness/rights file
a supporting-cast car's borderline status is challenged

base.update_signal: a new car proposal or a marque trademark-status clarification changes the canon

nodes.definition: Fix the flash tier that is OUT of genre except as a rare contrast beat. Modern hypercars and wrap-culture cars (Lamborghini in lime/orange, chrome wraps, gold Bugattis, widebody kits), rev-bombing exhaust content, and dealership-flex framing photograph as "new money loud" and break the classic read [ESTIMATE - high confidence, basis the loud-luxury definition and quiet-luxury press]. Modern Ferrari/Lamborghini in dark solid colors can pass in a Monaco-night beat, but the default is no [ESTIMATE - medium].

included: the rare dark-solid Monaco-night exception and its default-no status
excluded: the classic-tier canon itself (its own node)
the on-camera treatment rules for cars that do get cast (its own node)

pros.claim: Naming the flash tier explicitly gives a casting director a fast reject list rather than relying on subjective 'does this feel classy' judgment

nodes.definition: Fix the on-camera treatment for cars. Shoot cars as objects of craft: detail close-ups (grille texture, hood ornament, gauge needles, leather stitching, wood wheel rim), slow orbital or tracking shots at golden hour, coastal/alpine roads, never parking-lot flex poses [ESTIMATE - high, basis the visual codes]. Colors: silver, ivory, navy, British racing green, burgundy - no wraps [ESTIMATE - high, same basis].

excluded: the flash-tier exclusion this treatment applies to (its own node)
the trademark caution on badges within these detail shots (its own node)

nodes.definition: Fix the trademark-caution cross-reference. Car grilles, badges, mascots (e.g. Spirit of Ecstasy) and model trade dress are protected marks; whether AI-generated commercial content may depict them, and how prominently, is a legal question answered in the likeness/rights research file - NOT here [ESTIMATE - high that this is the conservative lane; law pinned elsewhere]. Default operating posture until that file says otherwise: badges/mascots de-emphasized or out of focus, no brand names in captions implying endorsement. The same treatment applies to watches (see WATCH_CANON): macro of dial/strap is fine, but brand-name captioning follows the same conservative default.

included: the protected-marks scope (grilles, badges, mascots, trade dress)
the default conservative posture (de-emphasize/out-of-focus, no endorsement-implying captions)
the explicit deferral to the likeness/rights file as the legal authority
excluded: the legal determination itself, which belongs to the likeness/rights research file, not this KB

pros.claim: Naming a conservative default posture lets production proceed today without waiting on a legal ruling, while staying safely inside the likely-conservative lane
pros.example: shooting a Rolls-Royce grille slightly soft-focus and uncaptioned rather than halting the shoot pending legal review

cons.claim: This node cannot itself resolve the legal question, so any shot involving a prominent, sharp, captioned badge remains genuinely unresolved risk

failure_modes: treating this KB's conservative default as if it were the legal answer itself
captioning a shot with a brand/model name in a way that implies endorsement

nodes.definition: Fix the watch canon. The classic-luxurious wrist = thin dress watches and heritage sports pieces - Patek Philippe Calatrava class, Cartier Tank class, Jaeger-LeCoultre Reverso class, vintage Rolex Datejust/Daytona class - on leather straps or subtle bracelets; no iced/gem-set pieces (gem-set = loud tier) [ESTIMATE - high, basis the materials/register codes]. On camera: macro of dial/strap, never wrist-to-lens flex pose. Trademark treatment follows the same conservative default as cars (see TRADEMARK_CAUTION_CROSSREF).

included: the four named watch classes and the strap/bracelet preference
excluded: male/female accessory canon beyond the watch itself (their own nodes)

nodes.definition: Fix the table-setting canon. Pressed white/cream linen, bone china (plain or thin gold rim), unlabeled decanters instead of bottle labels, polished (not ornate) silverware, low single-stem or no florals, real candles [ESTIMATE - high, basis the material codes]. nodes.definition: Fix the branding/saturation/clutter gauche tells. Logo spam/prominent branding is the defining loud-luxury marker; quiet luxury hides branding [FACT - Wikipedia; Baltini]. Oversaturated, too-bright color reads cheap/commercial and off-register for high-end photography [FACT - pixelphant.com]. Clutter/design noise/no negative space is a named luxury-branding failure [FACT - katemale.com; pixelphant.com]. Gradient-heavy, ornament-stuffed graphics/logos on cards and covers are named failures [FACT - digiquack.com; mediaboom.com]. These four are treated as one QC category because they all instantiate the same "restraint is the signal" principle broken.

excluded: the light/material gauche tells (its own node)

nodes.definition: Fix the light and material gauche tells. Harsh direct light too close, unfilled hard shadows, mixed color temperatures read as "cheap light"; controlled soft purposeful light is the high-end marker [FACT - pixelphant.com]. Plastic/synthetic surfaces in frame (acrylic chairs, PVC, glossy laminate, polyester sheen) violate the material canon [ESTIMATE - high]. Too-new everything - showroom-condition props with zero patina - reads staged; wabi-sabi patina reads owned [ESTIMATE - high, basis the Kyoto ryokan sourcing on patina-as-beauty].

nodes.definition: Fix the flex-grammar and casting gauche tells. Flex grammar: cash fans, bottle-service sparklers, watch-to-lens poses, "look at my car badge" framing, private-jet-door selfie cliché [ESTIMATE - high]. conflict_axes.name: quiet_vs_loud_luxury_register
conflict_axes.description: The central genre tension: quiet-luxury restraint versus loud-luxury flash, with loud elements only permitted as a rare deliberate contrast beat.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: quiet wins by default; loud elements require an explicit rare-contrast-beat designation

conflict_axes.name: trend_chasing_vs_timeless_grammar
conflict_axes.description: Fashion press already called peak quiet-luxury outdated by 2024, tempting either abandonment of the codes or over-indexing on a dated 2023-specific reference.
poles: treat quiet luxury as a fading 2023 trend
treat quiet luxury as a durable decades-old grammar
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: adopt the underlying decades-old codes as timeless grammar while dropping any single dated trend-specific reference

conflict_axes.name: restraint_vs_premium_combination_richness
conflict_axes.description: The palette's restraint principle can be undercut by applying a named three-color premium combination at full saturation/weight.
poles: apply a named combination at full richness
apply the restraint principle's single-accent cap
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: use a named combination as one anchor plus a restrained accent, never all its colors at equal weight

conflict_axes.name: craft_detail_focus_vs_trademark_deemphasis
conflict_axes.description: Shooting cars/watches as objects of craft calls for tight detail close-ups, which conflicts with de-emphasizing badges/mascots for trademark caution.
poles: shoot every detail in tack-sharp focus
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: shoot craft texture in focus but keep badges/mascots/trade dress soft-focus or cropped, pending the likeness/rights file

conflict_axes.name: classic_car_heritage_vs_modern_hypercar_exception
conflict_axes.description: The classic tier is the default car canon, but a rare dark-solid modern-hypercar exception is allowed for a Monaco-night beat.
poles: cast only from the classic-tier canon
allow a modern-hypercar exception for a specific beat
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: default to the classic tier; the modern exception requires dark solid color and a Monaco-night context, never a default choice

conflict_axes.name: serif_type_authority_vs_vendor_reported_stat_caution
conflict_axes.description: The Monotype perception-uplift figures are vendor-published, not independently verified, yet still useful directional guidance for the typography system.
poles: cite the vendor figures as independently verified
discard the vendor figures entirely for lack of independent verification
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: keep the serif-lineage convention and cite the figures with an explicit vendor-reported caveat, neither overstating nor discarding them

conflict_axes.name: patina_as_luxury_vs_too_new_showroom_tell
conflict_axes.description: Wabi-sabi patina reads as owned and luxurious, while pristine, showroom-new props read as staged or AI-generated.
poles: dress the set with pristine, new-condition props
dress the set with aged, patina-bearing props
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: prefer aged/worn/hand-finished versions of props and surfaces over showroom-pristine ones

conflict_axes.name: generic_archetype_safety_vs_named_brand_specificity
conflict_axes.description: Naming a specific trademarked marque/model/venue is more evocative than a generic description, but raises unresolved trademark risk this KB defers.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: default to the generic archetype description; only use a specific named mark once the likeness/rights file clears it

treat every tell as a generic AI-artifact owned by realism/QC

edge_cases.description: AI-specific luxury killers (waxy skin against real linen, warped serif signage, gold rendered as yellow plastic) can look like a styling mistake rather than a generation artifact
edge_cases.trigger: a produced shot shows one of the five named luxury-specific AI-artifact intersections
edge_cases.mitigation: route it to the realism/QC specialist's artifact taxonomy rather than treating it as a re-stylable gauche tell alone

edge_cases.description: A scene stacks more than one named premium color combination (e.g. black+gold+ivory and navy+platinum+cream) in a single frame
edge_cases.trigger: two or more of the three named combinations appear together in one shot
edge_cases.mitigation: restrict any one shot to a single combination plus neutrals per the restraint principle

workflow.action: Confirm the shot concept sits in the quiet-luxury register
workflow.description: Check the proposed concept against the quiet-vs-loud definitional split before any styling decision proceeds
workflow.gate: the concept is confirmed quiet-luxury or explicitly flagged as a rare contrast beat

workflow.action: Frame the shot's brief around identity and heritage, not a product pitch
workflow.description: State what identity/heritage the shot communicates rather than what feature or price it sells
workflow.gate: the brief names an identity/heritage beat, not a product-feature pitch

workflow.action: Select set/wardrobe materials from the whitelist
workflow.description: Choose materials for the scene's set dressing and wardrobe from the sourced whitelist
workflow.gate: every selected material appears on or is classified against the whitelist

workflow.action: Screen the selection against the materials blacklist
workflow.description: Check the chosen materials for any blacklisted plastic/synthetic/chrome-everything surface before shooting
workflow.gate: no blacklisted material survives into the shot

workflow.action: Set the base palette to neutrals plus one deep anchor plus a restrained metallic accent
workflow.description: Lock the scene's grade to the restraint principle with the accent capped under 5% of frame
workflow.gate: the accent coverage is confirmed under the 5% cap

workflow.action: Typeset any cover card or on-screen text per the serif/white-space rules
workflow.description: Apply the one-serif-family, no-more-than-2-size, under-20%-frame text rules to any card or caption
workflow.gate: the card meets the type-size, gradient, and frame-coverage rules

workflow.action: Compose the frame for negative space and a low prop count
workflow.description: Apply the symmetry/negative-space/3-5-object-cap rules to the shot's composition
workflow.gate: the frame's significant-object count is at or under 5

workflow.action: Cast the car from the classic-luxurious tier if the beat features one
workflow.description: Select a marque/era from the named core canon or its supporting cast
workflow.gate: the chosen car is on the classic-tier or supporting-cast list, or an explicit flash-tier exception is documented

workflow.action: De-emphasize badges, mascots, and trade dress on any car, watch, or branded prop
workflow.description: Apply the conservative default posture to any detail shot involving a protected mark
workflow.gate: no protected badge/mascot/trade dress sits in tack-sharp central focus

workflow.action: Run the gauche-tell QC pass for branding, saturation, and clutter
workflow.description: Check the shot for logo spam, oversaturation, design noise, and gradient-heavy graphics
workflow.gate: none of the four named failures is present

workflow.action: Hand off remaining AI-specific luxury killers to the realism/QC specialist
workflow.description: Flag any of the five named luxury-specific AI-artifact intersections and route them to the realism/QC specialist's own taxonomy
workflow.gate: every flagged intersection is routed, not resolved as a styling fix alone

dominance_rules.rule: The quiet-luxury register dominates a loud-luxury flourish by default
dominance_rules.rationale: the genre lock names loud elements as out of genre except for a rare deliberate contrast beat
dominance_rules.trigger: a styling choice reads flashy or loud
dominance_rules.action: revert to the quiet-luxury default unless the choice is explicitly marked a rare contrast beat

dominance_rules.rule: The classic-tier car canon dominates a modern-hypercar choice by default
dominance_rules.rationale: the flash tier is defined as breaking the classic read except for a rare, tightly-scoped exception
dominance_rules.trigger: a car beat is being cast
dominance_rules.action: choose from the classic-tier canon unless a signed-off dark-solid Monaco-night exception applies

dominance_rules.rule: Trademark caution dominates tight badge/mascot framing
dominance_rules.rationale: car grilles, badges, mascots and trade dress are protected marks whose depiction is legally unresolved here
dominance_rules.trigger: a detail shot crops tight on a badge, mascot, or brand mark
dominance_rules.action: keep the mark out of tack-sharp focus pending the likeness/rights file's determination

dominance_rules.rule: Restraint dominates stacking multiple premium color combinations
dominance_rules.rationale: fewer colors equal higher perceived value, and stacking combinations breaks that restraint signal
dominance_rules.trigger: more than one named premium combination appears in the same frame
dominance_rules.action: drop to a single combination plus neutrals

dominance_rules.rule: A FACT-tagged claim dominates an ESTIMATE-tagged craft-synthesis claim when stating confidence
dominance_rules.rationale: the content-discipline honesty contract requires the confidence label to travel with the claim rather than be smoothed over
dominance_rules.trigger: a FACT-tagged claim and an ESTIMATE-tagged claim co-occur in the same guidance
dominance_rules.action: state the FACT plainly and flag the ESTIMATE's confidence level explicitly, never upgrading it to FACT

dominance_rules.rationale: wabi-sabi patina reads as owned while a pristine, zero-patina prop reads as staged or AI-generated
dominance_rules.trigger: a prop or surface is being chosen for a shot
dominance_rules.action: prefer an aged, worn, or hand-finished version over a showroom-pristine one

dominance_rules.rule: Unbranded or unlabeled props dominate branded-label props
dominance_rules.rationale: logo spam is the defining loud-luxury marker and quiet luxury hides branding
dominance_rules.trigger: a bottle, bag, or garment could show a visible brand label or logo
dominance_rules.action: use the unlabeled/unbranded version or angle the label out of frame

dominance_rules.rule: A generic location/archetype description dominates naming a specific trademarked property
dominance_rules.rationale: the trademark/venue-naming boundary is deferred to the likeness/rights research file, not resolved here
dominance_rules.trigger: a location prompt could name a specific trademarked hotel, villa, or venue
dominance_rules.action: use the generic archetype description instead

dominance_rules.rule: The realism/QC handoff dominates treating an AI artifact as a pure styling mistake
dominance_rules.rationale: the artifact taxonomy proper is a distinct expert domain owned by the realism/QC specialist
dominance_rules.trigger: a tell looks like both a styling gauche-tell and a generation artifact
dominance_rules.action: route it to the realism/QC specialist's taxonomy rather than only re-styling the shot

anti_rework_rules.rule: Lock the register and base palette before wardrobe/prop sourcing begins
anti_rework_rules.prevents: sourcing props in a register or color scheme that gets discarded once the palette is formally set

anti_rework_rules.rule: Confirm the car's era/tier before scheduling a location and light plan built around it
anti_rework_rules.prevents: redesigning a golden-hour/coastal-road light plan after a flash-tier car gets swapped out for a classic-tier one

anti_rework_rules.rule: Check trademark caution on any car/watch/branded prop before the detail-shot list is finalized
anti_rework_rules.prevents: reshooting close-ups that must be recropped or re-angled later to de-emphasize a badge

anti_rework_rules.rule: Confirm the typography rules before designing a cover-card layout
anti_rework_rules.prevents: re-typesetting a card after a gradient or a second typeface gets flagged as a gauche tell

anti_rework_rules.rule: Screen materials against the blacklist before set dressing is purchased or rendered
anti_rework_rules.prevents: re-dressing a set after acrylic or glossy-laminate props get flagged in QC

anti_rework_rules.rule: Decide the single palette combination before color-grading begins
anti_rework_rules.prevents: re-grading footage that was shot with two named combinations stacked in one frame

anti_rework_rules.rule: Verify a car color and paint finish against the classic-tier muted-color rule before principal photography
anti_rework_rules.prevents: reshooting a car beat because a bright or wrapped finish broke the classic read

anti_rework_rules.rule: Run the gauche-tell QC pass before handing a shot to the realism/QC specialist
anti_rework_rules.prevents: the realism specialist re-flagging a purely stylistic, non-AI mistake that this KB's own rubric should have caught first

iteration_protocol.trigger: fashion press further declares quiet luxury dated beyond the 2024 trend-fade note
iteration_protocol.action: re-verify the timeless-grammar framing still holds or adjust the register lock accordingly

iteration_protocol.trigger: the likeness/rights research file resolves the named-venue/trademark boundary
iteration_protocol.action: update the trademark-caution cross-reference and any location/car/watch naming defaults

iteration_protocol.trigger: Monotype or an independent study publishes a verified, non-vendor typography-perception figure
iteration_protocol.action: replace the vendor-reported +13%/+9% caveat with the verified figure

iteration_protocol.trigger: a new car era or model is proposed for the canon
iteration_protocol.action: classify it against the classic-vs-flash tier criteria before approving it for a shoot

iteration_protocol.trigger: the realism/QC specialist's artifact taxonomy publishes a new tell relevant to luxury materials or surfaces
iteration_protocol.action: add it to the realism-QC handoff node's luxury-specific intersection list

iteration_protocol.trigger: a produced shot is found to break the luxury read despite passing this KB's rubric
iteration_protocol.action: add the missed tell as a new gauche-tell instance and re-derive the QC ordering

iteration_protocol.trigger: a new quiet-luxury fashion house, watch class, or car marque becomes canonical in press coverage
iteration_protocol.action: evaluate it against the register lock before adding it to the whitelist/canon

priority_rationale: The register-lock and luxury-strategy-theory foundations come first because every material, palette, typography, car, and accessory rule is a specialization of the quiet-vs-loud definition and the identity-over-features framing; materials and palette come next because typography, composition, cars, watches, accessories and table settings all draw from the same whitelist/restraint-principle base; the car canon and its trademark cross-reference follow because watches inherit the same trademark posture; the gauche-tell nodes come after every canon they invert against; and the realism-QC handoff comes last because it composes all three gauche-tell categories into the cross-reference the realism specialist's own artifact taxonomy builds on.
